subject: Unexpected billing spike from model routing multipliers / invoice hold request
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@epayments.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Accounting Team <acct@epayments.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Apr 2028 08:17:00 -0400
Subject: Re: April invoice spike - immediate hold requested

Hi Markus,

We reviewed the April invoice and see a ~480% jump in per-token charges compared to our March baseline. Charge line: invoice 2028-04-01 shows two line items with near-identical timestamps (2028-04-07T14:22Z) for the same API patterns; attached are the sample rows from our export with request_ids. Examples: req-9f3a, req-9f3b, req-9f3c. Each shows identical prompt length but token_captured values are ~2x what we expect.

This is material for our finance team; we've put the payment on hold for the disputed portion pending explanation. We also need to confirm VAT handling: EPayments is EU-registered and expects a reverse-charge (no VAT on your side). The invoice currently lists standard VAT.

Can you provide: 1) per-request evidence for the highlighted request_ids, 2) explanation for the multiplier and whether this was an engine routing behavior (fallback/dual-routing), and 3) an ETA for a reconciled invoice/credit note?

We'd like to resolve quickly — please put us in touch with billing and ops so we can avoid a wider collection hold.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of Platform Operations
EPayments Inc.
attachments: sample-usage-rows.csv

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@epayments.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Apr 2028 09:01:00 -0400
Subject: Re: April invoice spike - immediate hold requested

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear examples and for flagging VAT. Sorry for the disruption. I'm looping in Ben from billing and Grace from customer success to triage.

Immediate steps:
- Ben: can you pull per-request accounting for req-9f3a/9f3b/9f3c and confirm whether tokens were double-counted or whether a high-cost model was used?
- Grace: we'll propose a temporary credit to remove the disputed portion while we investigate; finance will need the per-request logs and a short narrative to reissue the invoice without VAT under reverse-charge.

Elena, we will treat this as a priority and aim to get preliminary findings within 24 hours. If you prefer, we can keep the invoice on hold until resolution. Let me know.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena@epayments.com>, Accounting Team <acct@epayments.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Apr 2028 13:46:00 -0400
Subject: Re: April invoice spike - immediate hold requested

Markus / Grace / Elena — quick triage and evidence pulled. Summary below, followed by attachments.

Summary of findings (preliminary):
- We examined router traces and tokenization logs for the three request_ids you provided. See attached sample-usage-rows.csv (subset) and router-trace-20280409.txt.
- For each request_id (req-9f3a, req-9f3b, req-9f3c) we observed a retry delivered by the smart-routing layer where the original request timed out waiting for a low-latency path and was retried to a fallback variant. The retry window overlapped with the original, and both responses were recorded and billed.
- The routing behavior is controlled by a per-account burst policy (your account is configured with aggressive fallback to maintain success rates during regional contention). That policy caused a duplicate execution in ~0.3% of requests during the 14:22 UTC window.
- The double-counted tokens match the surplus on the invoice once we aggregate across the affected time window.

What we propose:
1) Issue a provisional credit equal to the double-counted tokens for the disputed invoice period. We estimate the credit at EUR 18,974.50 based on our sample extrapolation; we will refine to an exact number once we finish the full export.
2) Reissue the invoice net of the credit and with reverse-charge VAT terms. We will prepare a credit note + corrected invoice (PDF) and send via DocuSign for your records.
3) Post-mitigation options: we can change your fallback policy to a conservative mode (less automatic retries) or add deduplication at the gateway for the specific 14:22–14:37 window. We recommend the conservative fallback for production and a short-term dedupe backfill if you want us to retroactively scrub the window.

Attachments included: sample-usage-rows.csv (3 rows for the request_ids), router-trace-20280409.txt (routing decisions and retry_count flags), proposed-credit-note-draft.pdf (draft credit note for quick review).

Next steps: Elena — if you confirm you'd like the provisional credit and the invoice reissue, we'll finalize the exact credit amount within 48 hours and send the revised invoice + DocuSign package. If you'd like a deeper forensic export, we can provide the full per-request dump (will take ~24 hours to generate).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Billing Analyst
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Rossi <elena@epayments.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.com>, Accounting Team <acct@epayments.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 14:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: April invoice spike - immediate hold requested

Thanks Ben — that summary answers our main questions and aligns with what we saw. EPayments confirms we would like the provisional credit and a reissued invoice without VAT under reverse-charge. Please go ahead with the credit calculation and send the DocuSign for the credit note.

Two small asks for compliance: 1) the credit note needs a short explanation line referencing "duplicate execution due to routing retry overlap" so our AP team can map it, and 2) include the list of canonical request_ids and the net token adjustment on the credit note PDF.

We will keep the disputed portion on hold until the corrected invoice is issued. Once we receive the DocuSign and the corrected invoice, we'll process the remainder of the balance.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of Platform Operations
EPayments Inc.
